title: Headings Hierarchy & Conventions
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 2
notes: Rules for the five heading levels: subject, main, group, paragraph and sub-paragraph headings.

rules.title: Subject heading: centred, bold capitals, no full stop
rules.description: Most documents start with a subject heading placed centrally in bold capitals, not followed by a full stop.

check.where: The first heading of the document.

autofix.description: Centre the subject heading, make it bold capitals, and remove any trailing full stop.

rules.title: Main heading: centred, bold capitals, 2 points larger
rules.description: A main heading is placed centrally over the typed area in bold capitals, not followed by a full stop, and is 2 points larger than the body text.

rules.title: Group heading: left margin, bold capitals, not numbered
rules.description: A group heading occupies a line by itself beginning at the left-hand margin, is not numbered and is not followed by a full stop. It is in bold capitals.

check.where: Group headings introducing one or more paragraphs on the same subject.

rules.title: Paragraph heading: bold, initial capitals, followed by full stop
rules.description: A paragraph heading is bold, uses capitals for the initial letters of all words except unimportant ones ('of', 'and', 'to', 'the', 'from'), and is followed by a full stop.

check.where: Paragraph headings covering a single paragraph and its sub-paragraphs.

rules.title: Once a paragraph heading is used, subsequent paragraphs must be headed
rules.description: Once a paragraph heading is used, succeeding paragraphs down to the next main or group heading must have headings.

check.where: Sequence of paragraphs between main/group headings.

rules.title: Headings must stand alone and not form part of a sentence
rules.description: Headings should stand on their own and not form part of any sentence that follows.

check.where: Heading text immediately followed by sentence continuation in the same paragraph.

rules.notes: Heuristic: flags headings whose first word after the full stop is lower case, suggesting the heading is embedded in a sentence.

rules.title: Two-line headings: second line shorter and centred
rules.description: In a 2-line main heading, if one line is necessarily shorter than the other, the second line is to be the shorter and placed centrally under the first.

rules.title: Sub-paragraph headings follow paragraph heading rules
rules.description: Sub-paragraph headings, and those of any further sub-divisions, follow rules similar to those for paragraph headings.
